analysis.investment_thesis: Bandhan Bank has recovered impressively from its FY22 near-wipeout (126 Cr profit) to 2,745 Cr in FY25, and forward P/E of 10.92x looks superficially cheap. But with ROE barely at 11% — below most estimates of equity cost — a P/B of 1.14x offers no margin of safety, and the MFI sector is entering another stress cycle.
key_strengths: Balance sheet has strengthened — total debt down from 24,711 Cr (FY23) to 11,138 Cr (FY25), equity up to 24,605 Cr
Net profit recovery from 126 Cr (FY22) to 2,745 Cr (FY25) demonstrates the franchise survived a severe stress event
P/B of 1.14x is near book — limited downside if earnings stabilize
key_risks: Finance costs growing at 26.6% CAGR (5,157 → 10,458 Cr in 3 years) vs. revenue CAGR of 7.8% — NIM compression structurally erodes profitability
Core MFI segment concentrated in Bengal/East India faces renewed stress in FY25-26 cycle as borrower overleveraging resurfaces across the sector
ROE of 11.16% barely covers cost of equity — intrinsic P/B approximates ROE/COE ≈ 0.9x, implying current price is modestly above intrinsic book value
red_flags: Promoter at 39.74% — RBI has been pushing Bandhan to reduce promoter concentration; regulatory overhang is persistent
Operating cash flow swings wildly: +902 Cr (FY22), -4,245 Cr (FY23), +14,808 Cr (FY24), +2,752 Cr (FY25) — predictability is low
Forward P/E of 10.92x assumes a substantial earnings jump that is far from assured given MFI sector headwinds and rising funding costs
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bandhan's core problem is structural, not cyclical: a microfinance-heavy book with a regionally concentrated customer base is inherently high-beta, and the market has correctly discounted this with a sub-1.2x P/B. The FY22 collapse to 126 Cr in profit was a stress-test that the bank passed, but only barely. The recovery looks spectacular on a percentage basis purely due to the low base, not because the underlying ROE profile has improved — 11% ROE in FY25 is roughly where it was pre-IPO.

The second-order question: what does the forward P/E of 10.92x require? It implies earnings approaching ~2,575 Cr+ on a normalized basis. That's achievable, but it's priced in. Any adverse development — another MFI stress cycle, rate hike, West Bengal political disruption — compresses earnings sharply. Risk/reward is roughly balanced. I neither want to pay up nor short it.
